input.quote: Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes two Customer-payable liquidated amounts, both expressly deemed "liquidated damages and not a penalty" by § 13.5: the § 11.1 Termination for Convenience Fee and the § 11.2(A) Termination for Cause Fee, each set at a REDACTED percentage of "Estimated Remaining Value" (months remaining to end of Term × the greater of the Monthly Base Fee or average monthly Fees) and each expressly carved out of the § 13.4 limitation. That fails every fallback element: there is more than one liquidated amount, one of them is triggered by Customer default rather than early termination, and the quantum is measured against the remaining contract value rather than capped at three months' fees — approaching walk-away territory. We therefore cap the fee at three months' average Fees, replace the Cause Fee with that same early-termination fee (preserving the § 11.1 payment mechanics and the unrelated Expenses reimbursement verbatim), and state in § 13.5 that it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer; the now-unused "Estimated Remaining Value" definition can be left in place or deleted. Noted but not redlined here: § 9.2(D) Service Level Credits running to Customer are REDACTED, so the reciprocal benefit is unverifiable; § 8.13 collection fees/Damages and default repricing to M&I's standard published prices are indemnity/pricing mechanics rather than liquidated amounts, and the new § 13.5 sentence confirms they are not additional liquidated damages. Quantum is argued once here rather than duplicated under the termination-for-convenience rule.

proposal.summary: Cap Customer-payable termination fee at three months' fees, replace the Termination for Cause Fee with that same early-termination fee, and make it the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our preferred position is that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties; as a fallback we accept a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. We therefore cap the Termination for Convenience Fee at three months' average Fees, replace the separate Termination for Cause Fee (a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value) with that same early-termination fee, and confirm in § 13.5 that it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.

ops.oldText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
ops.newText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to three (3) times the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three (3) months prior to the Effective Date of Termination.

ops.oldText: then Customer shall pay M&I a termination fee ("Termination for Cause Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value, payable as set forth in Section 11.1 above. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer. The Termination for Cause Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4.
ops.newText: then Customer shall pay M&I the Termination for Convenience Fee determined and payable as set forth in Section 11.1 above, and no other termination fee, liquidated damages or penalty. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer.

ops.newText: Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee is a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty. The Termination for Convenience Fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement.
